transcript: The other night, I attended a solo piece by Sam Kissajukian called 300 Paintings at Vineyard Theatre. In direct address to the audience, Sam walks us through a midlife crisis that involved quitting comedy, picking up painting, and also a slight detour into inventing. All of this coincides with his bipolar diagnosis and its aftermath. Sam's humor and thoughtful insights around mental health as it relates to artistry and creativity, coupled with an eclectic set of visual references on a slideshow, makes this feel kind of like an extended TED Talk. It's personal but I think it would resonate with artists of any medium and leaves you with a solid message or thesis statement, so to speak. I think this piece would be especially enjoyable for visual artists as Sam's paintings are quite good and are featured throughout the lobby for the audience to peruse and admire afterwards. With that, another program for my collection.
